title: A development server that assumed loopback binds to every interface, and its convenience endpoint is unauthenticated
index_line: T-0063 · EXEC · Metro's /open-url accepts a POST that runs a command, on a server bound to 0.0.0.0 · node · corroborated
invariant_violated: Developer tooling is assumed to be local: it listens on a port for the developer's own machine, so nobody thought about who else could reach it. But the default bind address is *all interfaces*, and the endpoints exist to do convenient things like open a URL — which on a desktop means handing a string to the shell.

mechanism.does: the developer runs the tool's development server, which binds to all interfaces by default
the server exposes helper endpoints with no authentication, including one that opens a URL on the host
an attacker who can reach the port posts a value to that endpoint
the handler passes the value to the platform's URL/command opener, which interprets shell syntax
the command runs as the developer on a machine that holds source, tokens and credentials

source.http.body.value: a JSON body with a `url`/`target` field — no token, no origin check

sink.exec.shell.value: the platform's open-a-URL helper, which on Windows resolves through cmd.exe

guard.none.value: no authentication, no origin check, and no restriction of the bind address

header.forwarding.value: the Host/Origin headers are the only things that could distinguish a local caller, and they are not consulted

preconditions.expr: the tool version is affected and its dev server binds broadly
the port is reachable from the attacker's position (shared network, container host, VPN)
an unauthenticated helper endpoint performs a host action

success: a POST to the helper endpoint spawns a shell child process on the developer machine
the server's status endpoint answers from a host that is not the developer's
the process tree shows cmd.exe or a shell under the dev-server process
failure_like: the server binds to 127.0.0.1 only, or the endpoint requires a token
false_positive: the dev server answering from another machine — that is reachability; the finding needs command execution
a firewall or container boundary that blocks the port: establish reachability before claiming it

hazards: every dev server in the chain is a candidate: bundlers, hot-reload servers, mock APIs, storybook, debug ports, notebook kernels
the default bind address is the whole bug — check `ss -lntp` on a developer machine and count what listens on 0.0.0.0
these hold no auth because their threat model was 'my own laptop'; on a shared network or a container host they are remote code execution
distinct from T-0058 (install-time hook) and T-0038 (CI tag): this one is a *listening service*, discovered by scanning rather than by pinning
non_transfers: dev servers that bind to loopback by default and require a token for host actions
isolated developer networks where the port is genuinely unreachable

evidence.target: React Native Community CLI Metro dev server (CVE-2025-11953, 'Metro4Shell')
